worker_boundary_rule: A region worker may rebuild interiors inside its frozen macro envelope and named-island scope. Missing land/islands must already have a declared macro association; uncovered source geometry is not evidence that the island does not exist.

new_sources.inspected_fact: Eurasian continental limits are conventional: Ural/Greater Caucasus or Kuma–Manych variants. North Aegean/Dodecanese Asian shelf associations are separately described.
Under Greater Caucasus watershed convention north=Ciscaucasia/Europe and south=Transcaucasia/Asia.
Mountain-range source retrieved and text screened; no new exact crest geometry was obtained.
Dodecanese including Rhodes/Kastellorizo are described as the former Italian Aegean islands; historical owner is separate from geographic association.

Published province-group macro-region tables corroborate North China including Inner Mongolia and Central/South China memberships. Atlas Taiwan/Penghu exception does not adopt political claims in the source table.
Physical plateau spans Mongolia plus Inner Mongolia/Xinjiang and Russian Transbaikal/Buryatia/Irkutsk portions.
Mongolia is an East Asian mountain/plateau territory between China and Russia; its state envelope is not the whole transnational plateau.
Strict Soviet Middle Asia excludes Kazakhstan; broader common Central Asia includes it. Geographic and cultural definitions vary.
WGSRPD West Asia excludes Arabia and includes Afghanistan; West Asia has multiple pragmatic definitions.
Broad physical Siberia extends from Urals to Pacific; there is no single precise universal definition.
Modern Far Eastern Federal District includes Sakha and added Buryatia/Zabaykalsky in 2018; current atlas is not that exact district.
Malesia is a variable floristic/biogeographical region; WGSRPD 2001 separated Papuasia.
Mainland Southeast Asia physically includes Peninsular Malaysia/Singapore, joined to Thailand via Kra isthmus.
Extended subcontinent association includes Bhutan/Nepal/Sri Lanka/Maldives; Afghanistan generally excluded.
Malta is central Mediterranean about80km from southern Italy; Malta plateau is Sicily–North Africa shelf association.
Japanese main/Ryukyu arcs are described; adjacent Kuril and Izu–Bonin–Mariana arcs need an explicit atlas reporting association.
Official six-zone reference framework; page explicitly records2002 Sikkim transfer to NEC but omits later Telangana/Ladakh successor names.
South Andhra/Telangana/Karnataka/Kerala/Tamil Nadu/Puducherry.
North Haryana/Himachal/Punjab/Rajasthan/Chandigarh/Delhi/Jammu Kashmir/Ladakh.
West Goa/Gujarat/Maharashtra/Dadra Nagar Haveli and Daman Diu.
Central Chhattisgarh/Madhya Pradesh/Uttar Pradesh/Uttarakhand.
East Bihar/Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal.
Eight NEC states: Assam/Arunachal/Manipur/Tripura/Mizoram/Meghalaya/Nagaland/Sikkim.
Siachen meltwaters feed Nubra then Shyok then Indus; an Indus reporting association does not resolve sovereignty.
Anatolia is the West Asian peninsula bounded by Black/Aegean/Mediterranean seas and separated from Thrace by TurkishStraits; eastern limit varies, sometimes all AsiaticTurkey.

Levant is an EasternMediterranean historical/geographic association with varying breadth, separate from modern political identity; Egypt/Iraq and Cyprus are included in some usages. Atlas specifies listed reference envelopes rather than asserting all definitions agree.

Mesopotamia is WestAsian TigrisEuphrates historical region corresponding roughly to Iraq, transitioning toward IranianPlateau; atlas uses whole sourced Iraq reference envelope, not exact drainage mask.

Physical IranianPlateau encompasses mostIran/allAfghanistan and partsPakistan westofIndus. Atlas Iranian/Afghan reporting branch includes lowmargins and excludes separately associatedPakistan; it is not the wholephysicalplateau.

Chagos is about500km southofMaldives and southernmost archipelago of ChagosLaccadive submarine ridge; geography supports named SouthAsianIndianOcean reporting association independently of disputed sovereignowner.

sources.inspected_fact: Eurasian continental limits are conventional: Ural/Greater Caucasus or Kuma–Manych variants. North Aegean/Dodecanese Asian shelf associations are separately described.
Under Greater Caucasus watershed convention north=Ciscaucasia/Europe and south=Transcaucasia/Asia.
Mountain-range source retrieved and text screened; no new exact crest geometry was obtained.
Dodecanese including Rhodes/Kastellorizo are described as the former Italian Aegean islands; historical owner is separate from geographic association.

Published province-group macro-region tables corroborate North China including Inner Mongolia and Central/South China memberships. Atlas Taiwan/Penghu exception does not adopt political claims in the source table.
Physical plateau spans Mongolia plus Inner Mongolia/Xinjiang and Russian Transbaikal/Buryatia/Irkutsk portions.
Mongolia is an East Asian mountain/plateau territory between China and Russia; its state envelope is not the whole transnational plateau.
Strict Soviet Middle Asia excludes Kazakhstan; broader common Central Asia includes it. Geographic and cultural definitions vary.
WGSRPD West Asia excludes Arabia and includes Afghanistan; West Asia has multiple pragmatic definitions.
Broad physical Siberia extends from Urals to Pacific; there is no single precise universal definition.
Modern Far Eastern Federal District includes Sakha and added Buryatia/Zabaykalsky in 2018; current atlas is not that exact district.
Malesia is a variable floristic/biogeographical region; WGSRPD 2001 separated Papuasia.
Mainland Southeast Asia physically includes Peninsular Malaysia/Singapore, joined to Thailand via Kra isthmus.
Extended subcontinent association includes Bhutan/Nepal/Sri Lanka/Maldives; Afghanistan generally excluded.
Malta is central Mediterranean about80km from southern Italy; Malta plateau is Sicily–North Africa shelf association.
Japanese main/Ryukyu arcs are described; adjacent Kuril and Izu–Bonin–Mariana arcs need an explicit atlas reporting association.
Official six-zone reference framework; page explicitly records2002 Sikkim transfer to NEC but omits later Telangana/Ladakh successor names.
South Andhra/Telangana/Karnataka/Kerala/Tamil Nadu/Puducherry.
North Haryana/Himachal/Punjab/Rajasthan/Chandigarh/Delhi/Jammu Kashmir/Ladakh.
West Goa/Gujarat/Maharashtra/Dadra Nagar Haveli and Daman Diu.
Central Chhattisgarh/Madhya Pradesh/Uttar Pradesh/Uttarakhand.
East Bihar/Jharkhand/Odisha/West Bengal.
Eight NEC states: Assam/Arunachal/Manipur/Tripura/Mizoram/Meghalaya/Nagaland/Sikkim.
Siachen meltwaters feed Nubra then Shyok then Indus; an Indus reporting association does not resolve sovereignty.
Anatolia is the West Asian peninsula bounded by Black/Aegean/Mediterranean seas and separated from Thrace by TurkishStraits; eastern limit varies, sometimes all AsiaticTurkey.

Levant is an EasternMediterranean historical/geographic association with varying breadth, separate from modern political identity; Egypt/Iraq and Cyprus are included in some usages. Atlas specifies listed reference envelopes rather than asserting all definitions agree.

Mesopotamia is WestAsian TigrisEuphrates historical region corresponding roughly to Iraq, transitioning toward IranianPlateau; atlas uses whole sourced Iraq reference envelope, not exact drainage mask.

Physical IranianPlateau encompasses mostIran/allAfghanistan and partsPakistan westofIndus. Atlas Iranian/Afghan reporting branch includes lowmargins and excludes separately associatedPakistan; it is not the wholephysicalplateau.

Chagos is about500km southofMaldives and southernmost archipelago of ChagosLaccadive submarine ridge; geography supports named SouthAsianIndianOcean reporting association independently of disputed sovereignowner.
